business_problem: MITRE needed a secure, shared AI environment that government sponsors and researchers could use to test advanced models across domains without duplicating infrastructure or weakening controls around sensitive data.
solution_summary: MITRE consolidated scattered accelerated-computing resources into the Federal AI Sandbox, a DGX SuperPOD-powered environment built to let U.S. agencies and researchers safely experiment with AI across cybersecurity, weather, benefits, and other public-interest workloads. The platform can deploy the latest open-source models while maintaining the controls needed for sensitive and classified information, giving thousands of internal researchers a shared environment instead of isolated projects. MITRE uses the same stack with NVIDIA Earth-2, NVIDIA Omniverse, and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo to train and visualize high-resolution weather models, and it pairs DGX SuperPOD training with edge systems and simulation in a three-computer architecture for ocean and autonomy work. By centralizing multimodal AI training and inference, the sandbox supports everything from satellite imagery analysis to cybersecurity foundation models and public-benefits automation.

data_flow: Government and MITRE datasets are brought into the sandbox for centralized model training on DGX SuperPOD systems, specialized workflows use Earth-2, PhysicsNeMo, and Omniverse for simulation and visualization, and resulting models are shared back to researchers and agency programs for operational use.
business_outcome: MITRE increased AI-compute performance by 300x, created a shared experimentation environment for thousands of researchers, advanced 1-kilometer weather forecasting over water, and accelerated work on cybersecurity and public-benefits AI use cases.
